title: Baška Voda Cost Guide 2027: Daily Budget & Prices
metaDescription: What Baška Voda costs in 2027: accommodation, meals, beach, transport and day trips in euros, with budget tips for each season.
content:
## How Much Does a Day in Baška Voda Cost?

Baška Voda is one of the cheaper towns on the Makarska Riviera. A mid-range daily budget for two people in July or August is about €200–300 with a hotel or good apartment, meals out and a few extras. In September, one traveller report puts a modest day at around €50 for three people. In summer the same lifestyle costs two to three times more. Treat the September figure as a floor for self-catering stays, not a typical hotel trip.

### Daily Budget by Travel Style

| Style | Per person per day (summer) | Per person per day (May, June, September) |
|---|---|---|
| Budget (apartment, self-catering, bakery lunch) | €45–65 | €30–45 |
| Mid-range (apartment or 3-star, one restaurant meal) | €80–120 | €60–90 |
| Comfortable (4-star hotel, restaurant dinners, activities) | €130–200 | €100–150 |

These are planning ranges built from typical accommodation rates and restaurant checks. Real totals depend mostly on the room.

## Accommodation Costs

Accommodation is the largest expense. The town has hundreds of private apartments and rooms, plus a smaller number of hotels along the seafront.

### Hotels

Booking data shows many hotels listed from roughly €70–100 per night for two adults. Averages are higher for stars and season: 3-star hotels average about €200+ per night in peak dates, and 4-star hotels around €250 or more. Hotel price comparison data shows high season (June–August) averaging roughly double the low season (December–February). Names with a beachfront position include Grand Hotel Slavia, Alemaris Resort, Aparthotel Milenij, Hotel Villa Bacchus and Family Resort Urania. Pinadria Camping Resort is the camping-style option.

### Apartments and Private Rooms

Apartments are the better value in most cases. A double studio or one-bedroom apartment runs about €50–90 per night in shoulder season and €90–150 in July and August. Many are within 150–400 m of Glavna beach or Podluka beach. Confirm the cleaning fee, air conditioning charge and parking before booking, since these can add €10–40 per stay.

### Tourist Tax

Every guest pays a tourist tax per night, set by each town. Across Croatia the range is €0.65–2.65 per person per night. Children under 12 are exempt and ages 12–18 pay half. Neighbouring Makarska charges €2.00 per night from 1 April to 30 September and €1.50 the rest of the year. Baška Voda charges a comparable amount, so budget about €2 per adult per night. Hotels show it as a separate line on the bill.

## Food and Drink Prices

Baška Voda is cheaper than Makarska or Hvar, but the waterfront is not cheap. The promenade by Obala Sv. Nikole has the highest prices and the most tourist traffic.

- **Restaurant dinner:** a seafood meal with wine and beer for three people comes to around €40 at a waterfront restaurant such as Palac. A comparable grilled fish dinner with salads and a jug of white wine at Restaurant Aga, near Osejava Forest Park's side of town toward Promajna, was also about €40 for three.
- **Per person:** expect €15–25 for a main course and a drink at a konoba. Whole grilled fish is priced by the kilo, usually €60–90 per kg in summer, so ask the price before ordering.
- **Cheap meals:** bakery burek or pizza slices cost about €2–4. A cappuccino is around €2–2.50.
- **Groceries:** the town has several supermarkets and a small market with fruit, vegetables and seafood. A self-catering day for two costs €15–25 in food.

**Opinion:** Skip the first row of the main promenade for dinner. The same fish costs less and tastes the same two streets back or in a village konoba toward Promajna.

## Beaches and Activities

### Beaches

The town's pebble beaches, including Glavna, Podluka and Nikolina, are free to enter. Sunbed and umbrella sets at beach bars usually cost €15–30 per day in July and August. A towel on the free pebble stretches costs nothing, and shade comes from the pine trees behind the beach.

### Day Trips and Excursions

- **Brač via the Makarska–Sumartin ferry:** foot passengers pay €4.10–6.40 each way, a standard car €18.70–27.00, and a crossing takes about 1 hour. Two adults with a car pay about €27–40 one way.
- **Boat trips and quad tours:** typically €40–80 per person for half-day excursions.
- **Makarska:** about 5 km away. It is a short, cheap bus ride or a walk along the coast path.
- **Biokovo and Brela:** Brela is just north of town, and the beaches there are also free.

## Transport and Parking

A car is useful but not required. Parking in July and August is the main extra cost. Many apartments include a space, and this is worth more than a small discount on the room rate. Public parking in the center is paid in peak season, usually €1–2 per hour. Local buses along the coastal road link Baška Voda with Makarska, Brela and Tučepi for a few euros per ride. Taxi transfers from Split Airport take about 55–60 minutes by road, and a private transfer costs roughly €90–130.

## Best Time to Visit for Lower Prices

- **Cheapest:** October to April, though many restaurants and beach bars close.
- **Best value:** late May, June and September. The sea is warm enough for swimming, and room prices drop by a third or more.
- **Most expensive:** the last week of July and first two weeks of August.

## Money-Saving Tips

1. Book apartments before March for the best choice in July and August.
2. Pick a place 300–500 m back from the seafront. It is quieter and often €20–30 cheaper per night.
3. Eat the main meal at midday. Many konobas have lower-priced lunch plates than evening menus.
4. Buy water and snacks in supermarkets, not beach kiosks.
5. Pay in euros by card. Croatia uses the euro, and card payments are widely accepted, though small konobas and market stalls may prefer cash.
6. Ask whether the tourist tax and final cleaning are included in the quoted price.

## Is Baška Voda Expensive?

By Adriatic standards it is moderate. It costs less than Hvar, Split or Dubrovnik, and about the same as or slightly under Makarska. Most visitors find it good value out of peak weeks, with a clear price jump in the two peak summer months.

faq.question: How much money do I need per day in Baška Voda?
faq.answer: Budget travellers need about €45–65 per person per day in summer and €30–45 in shoulder season if they stay in apartments and self-cater. A mid-range trip with restaurant dinners costs €80–120 per person per day in summer. Accommodation makes up most of the total.

faq.question: Is Baška Voda cheaper than Makarska?
faq.answer: Generally yes, slightly. Apartments and restaurant meals cost a little less in Baška Voda, and the town is quieter. Makarska charges a tourist tax of €2.00 per night in high season, and Baška Voda is in a similar range.

faq.question: How much does a hotel cost in Baška Voda?
faq.answer: Hotels are listed from about €70–100 per night for two in low and shoulder season. Peak July and August rates for 3- and 4-star beachfront hotels are often €150–250 or more. Apartments are usually cheaper at €50–150.

faq.question: Are the beaches in Baška Voda free?
faq.answer: Yes. The public pebble beaches, including Glavna, Podluka and Nikolina, are free to enter. Only sunbeds and umbrellas cost money, usually €15–30 per set per day in peak summer.

faq.question: How much does the ferry from Makarska to Brač cost?
faq.answer: The Jadrolinija line 638 ferry from Makarska to Sumartin costs €4.10–6.40 for an adult and €18.70–27.00 for a standard car. The crossing takes about 1 hour. Check the live price for your date, since the fare changes by season.

faq.question: How much is a restaurant meal in Baška Voda?
faq.answer: A main course with a drink costs about €15–25 per person at a konoba. A fish dinner with wine for three people comes to around €40 in the waterfront restaurants reviewed. Whole fish is priced per kilo, so confirm the price before ordering.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Baška Voda?
faq.answer: November to April has the lowest prices, but many venues are closed. For good weather and lower costs, late May, June and September are the best choices, with accommodation often a third cheaper than in peak summer.

quickAnswer: Baška Voda costs roughly €60–90 per person per day in budget mode and €120–200 in peak summer with a mid-range hotel. Rooms and apartments run €50–150 per night depending on season, a restaurant meal is €15–25, and the beaches are free. Prices fall noticeably in May, June and September.
